review.summary: Across the central Arctic's thickest multi-year sea ice, Netsilingmiut Inuit perfected composite salmon leisters at stone river weirs, complex seal breathing-hole hunting systems, and winter snow-house neighborhoods along Boothia and Simpson Peninsula.
review.limitations: Permafrost organic preservation varies across raised gravel beaches vs. sod middens, and marine-mammal radiocarbon samples require Delta-R reservoir corrections; dates reflect scholarly consensus envelopes.
review.discussion: Distinguishes Paleo-Inuit traditions (Independence I, Pre-Dorset, Dorset/Tuniit) from later Thule–Inuit populations in accordance with archaeological and ancient genomic evidence, while centering Indigenous continuity to 1900 CE.
